title: NSF-Funded $11M CSTA AI Teacher Training Program Launches Across Six US States — Targeting Rural and Under-Resourced Schools
detail: The Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA), funded by an $11-million National Science Foundation grant, launched a comprehensive AI teacher professional development program covering Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, New Jersey, and South Carolina. The initiative runs 'AI PD Weeks' from June through August 2026, providing structured AI literacy, pedagogical integration, and ethical reasoning training for K-12 computer science teachers. The program is aligned with the executive order on 'Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth' and explicitly addresses equity gaps: participating states were selected to include high proportions of under-resourced schools and rural districts where AI education would otherwise be absent. The initiative targets teacher multiplier effects — each trained teacher is projected to reach 100+ students annually — meaning the $11M investment could translate into hundreds of thousands of students gaining AI literacy access. The program also launches a cohort of 20 AI Fellows (following SUNY's systemwide AI policy adopted May 2026) to provide ongoing support for faculty integrating AI into curricula. This NSF investment represents a major scaling of public AI education infrastructure in the United States, moving beyond urban tech-hub pilot programs into rural and under-resourced communities.
